Claude Sonnet is checking the tests of the commit and writing the missing ones...
hooks.prompt:
A git command just ran in this portfolio repository (Eleventy, Nunjucks, vanilla JS, Netlify functions in .mts). Its tool call and output, as JSON: $ARGUMENTS

Your job: make sure the code of the commit it created is covered by a unit, integration or E2E test, and write the missing tests.

Step 1. If the command created no commit (git commit --dry-run, nothing to commit, an amend that only rewords, or git commit only as text in a string), answer ok true and stop.
Step 2. Run git show --name-status --format= HEAD to list the committed files. Keep the code files: *.js, *.mjs, *.cjs, *.ts, *.mts, *.njk, *.html, *.css. Ignore deleted files, *.min.js and *.min.css, vendor libraries, config files (*.config.js, eslint / stylelint / jest / playwright configs), everything under .claude/, docs/, reports/ and node_modules/, and the test files themselves. If no code file is left, answer ok true and stop.
Step 3. For each code file, look for an existing test that covers it, wherever it is and whenever it was written: Jest tests (*.test.js / *.spec.js under js/ or netlify/, the Jest roots), Playwright tests (tests/*.spec.js), Cypress tests (cypress/**). A test covers a file when it imports it, or exercises the page, template, selector or feature it changes. If every code file is covered, answer ok true and stop.
Step 4. For each uncovered feature, write the most fitting test: a Jest unit test next to the code (js/<name>.test.js, netlify/functions/<name>.test.js) for functions and logic you can import; a Playwright integration or E2E test in tests/<name>.spec.js for page behaviour, templates and styles. Playwright has no webServer nor baseURL configured: build the site with npx @11ty/eleventy if needed and serve the output folder from the test (a small node:http static server started in beforeAll), the way the repository already serves pages elsewhere. Read jest.config.js, playwright.config.js and package.json first and follow the repository conventions. Test real behaviour, not implementation details; one focused test file per feature is enough.
Step 5. Run each new test (npx jest <file>, or npx playwright test <file> --project=Chromium) and fix the test until it passes. Never change the code under test to make a test pass; if a test reveals a real bug, keep the test, mark it test.fail or test.skip with a single-line comment naming the bug, and report it.
Rules: comments are single-line only, with no numbered lists in them; match the style of the surrounding code; do not stage, commit or push anything; do not touch css/app.css or any file other than the new tests.

Answer ok true when nothing had to be written. When you wrote tests, answer ok false with as reason one short paragraph for the developer: the test files you created (left untracked, to review and commit), what each covers, whether they pass, and any bug found.
